missing_methods.intent: Assert tell your experience text is truncated to 2000 characters
missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should: 1) Retrieve the current text from the feedback text edit field using get_entered_text(). 2) Calculate the actual length of the retrieved text. 3) Assert that the length does not exceed the expected_max_length parameter (default 2000). 4) Return True if the assertion passes, raise an AssertionError with a descriptive message if it fails. 5) The method should handle edge cases where the text field is empty or contains special characters. 6) Log the actual character count and the maximum allowed for debugging purposes.
implementation_checklist: Wait for 'edit_feedback' element to be present using self.driver.wait_for_object('edit_feedback')
Call existing get_entered_text() method to retrieve current text value from the feedback field
Store the retrieved text in a variable (e.g., actual_text)
Calculate the actual character count using len(actual_text)
Log the actual character count for debugging (e.g., using print or logger)
Wait for 'edit_feedback_char_count' element to be present using self.driver.wait_for_object('edit_feedback_char_count')
Get the character count display text using self.driver.get_attribute('edit_feedback_char_count', 'Name')
Parse the character count display to extract current count (e.g., from '2000/2000' format)
Assert that len(actual_text) <= expected_max_length using assert statement
Assert that len(actual_text) == expected_max_length for truncation verification
If assertion fails, raise AssertionError with descriptive message including actual length and expected max length
Handle edge case: if actual_text is None or empty string, log appropriately
Verify that the character count display matches the actual text length
Return True if all assertions pass successfully
